f.title: Consider newly identified issues, changed reactions and clinically significant toxicities in the risk evaluation
f.statement: Relevant points to consider in evaluating the risks include (where applicable): newly identified safety issues (detailed description of adverse events or reactions; associated laboratory values; risk factors; relationship to dose, duration, time course of the treatment; reversibility; factors that could be useful in predicting or preventing reactions); meaningful changes in previously identified adverse reactions (e.g., increased frequency or severity, outcome, specific at-risk populations); and symptoms, signs and laboratory evidence of newly and previously identified clinically significant toxicities (e.g., hepatotoxicity; cardiovascular effects including QT interval prolongation and results from thorough QT/QTc studies; bone marrow, pulmonary, renal and central nervous system toxicity; immunogenicity and hypersensitivity).
